messages.content:
Policy: Protected Health Information
Definition: No person-identifiable data or confidential business data may be input into public AI tools. Anonymization of data must be carefully assessed.
Policy Type: B

Candidate risks:
- 1: Compromise of privacy by obtaining, leaking or correctly inferring sensitive information — AI systems that memorize and leak sensitive personal data or infer private information about individuals without their consent. Unexpected or unauthorized sharing of data and information can compromise user expectation of privacy, assist identity theft, or loss of confidential intellectual property.
  Cross-mappings: credo-risk-036[close], ail-intellectual-property[related], ail-nonviolent-crimes[related]
- 2: Non-disclosure — Content might not be clearly disclosed as AI generated. (Concern: Users must be notified when they are interacting with an AI system. Not disclosing the AI-authored content can result in a lack of transparency.)
  Cross-mappings: nist-human-ai-configuration[broad], mit-ai-causal-risk-entity-human[related], mit-ai-causal-risk-intent-other[related]
- 3: Data usage rights restrictions — Terms of service, license compliance, or other IP issues may restrict the ability to use certain data for building models. (Concern: Laws and regulations concerning the use of data to train AI are unsettled and can vary from country to country, which creates challenges in the development of models.)
  Cross-mappings: llm032025-supply-chain[broad], nist-data-privacy[broad], nist-value-chain-and-component-integration[broad]
- 4: Sharing IP/PI/confidential information with tools — AI agents with unrestricted access to resources or databases or tools could potentially store and share PI/IP/confidential information with other tools or agents when performing their actions. (Concern: AI agents may share privileged information with other tools/agents. The act of sharing the information may result in harm for the model owner, user, or others. The harm can vary based on the type and details of the information shared. Without adequate oversight, these privacy incidents might overwhelm company resources.)
- 5: Compromised personally identifiable information (Slattery et al., 2024) — The AI system may expose personally identifiable information (PII), either inadvertently or due to adversarial inputs, derived from training data, accessible data, or inferences. PII is any data that can be used to directly identify or contact a specific individual, either alone or in combination with other information.
  Cross-mappings: mit-ai-risk-subdomain-2.1[close], ail-privacy[related], ail-specialized-advice[related]

matched_risks.justification: Directly addresses the policy concern of protecting person-identifiable data from leakage or inference.
Relates to the policy's emphasis on restricting input of confidential data into public AI tools.
